name: Insyta Click Tracker
author: toptima

sections.description:
Insyta Click Tracker records every click on a link or button on your site, together with the UTM parameters (source, medium, campaign, content, term) that brought the visitor in.

What it tracks (100% free, no account or license required):

  • Clicks on links and buttons, with the visible text and target URL
  • UTM source / medium / campaign / content / term
  • Basic device and browser
  • A simple dashboard: most-clicked links, top campaigns, recent activity

What it does not do:

  • No cookies required for tracking to work (UTM is only kept in sessionStorage for the current browser tab, never sent anywhere else)
  • No external service calls — all data is stored in your own WordPress database
  • No user accounts, emails, or IP addresses are stored

Need more?

Insyta Pro (a separate, paid product at insyta.io) adds heatmaps, session recording, rage/dead-click detection, scroll depth, conversion funnels, A/B testing and scheduled email reports. This free plugin does not require Pro and works completely on its own.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/insyta-click-tracker, or install directly from the WordPress plugin directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen.
  3. Go to Click Tracker in the admin menu to see your data once visitors start clicking.
sections.faq:
Does this slow down my site?

No. The tracker is a small script that only sends data when a visitor actually clicks something, using navigator.sendBeacon where available so it never blocks page rendering.

Where is the data stored?

In your own WordPress database, in a single table (wp_ict_clicks). Nothing is sent to any external server.

How long is data kept?

90 days by default, cleaned up automatically once a day. (Configurable in a future version.)

Does it work with page builders (Elementor, Bricks, etc.)?

Yes — it listens for clicks on any link or button on the page, regardless of which builder created it.
